facts.subject: EP-1 /api/health/auth
facts.measured: GET (:9) calls createClient() then supabase.auth.getUser() (:13) and branches on userError ALONE (:15). Any returned error - whatever its cause - yields 503 with {status:'degraded', authenticated:false, message:'Authentication service unavailable'} (:16-21). Success yields 200 {status:'ok', authenticated:!!user} (:24-28). A throw yields 500 (:29-35).
facts.consequence: An ANONYMOUS caller receives 503. @supabase/ssr returns AuthSessionMissingError in `error` for a cookieless request, so AS-1 takes the 503 branch. This is the state the ratified taxonomy records as AS-1 answered_today: 'EP-1 503', and it is the behaviour docs/ops/release/RELEASE_GATE_LEDGER_v1.0.0.json GATES[M11].measured_at_base.blocking_contract_conflict records production as exhibiting.
facts.absent: No AS-1..AS-4 discriminator. No provider-health touch. No cache. No TTL. No budget. No unauthenticated body distinguishing reachable from unreachable.

facts.subject: EP-2 /api/health/runtime-identity
facts.measured: Session-gated at :49 via getVerifiedAuthIdentityResult(). No identity -> 503 when failure === 'AUTH_UNAVAILABLE', else 401 (:57-60). With identity: 200 when payload.verified, else 503 (:70). Catch -> 503 with unobservableRuntimeIdentityPayload() (:77).
facts.consequence: Anonymous answer is 401, which the ratified matrix records as the CONFORMANT anonymous cell. Track A must not change it - MG-4.

facts.subject: EP-3 /api/health/stella-preconditions
facts.measured: Session-gated at :67 with the same 503/401 shape (:70-73). Payload (:82-118) already publishes master.stellaEnabled (:86), master.geminiApiKeyPresent (:88), master.canUseStella (:89), model.*, capabilities (:102), rateLimit (:103) and ready (:117). Status is exactly `payload.ready ? 200 : 503` (:123).
facts.consequence: The status collapses intentional-off with misconfigured; the BODY already distinguishes them. This is precisely the state OD-3 ratifies as SPLIT_STATUS_200_FOR_INTENTIONAL_OFF, and confirms the ratification's 'No new body field is required'.

facts.subject: The auth-failure discriminator - FIS-M11-01's site
facts.measured: lib/auth/identity.ts declares AuthIdentityFailure = NO_SESSION | SESSION_REJECTED | MALFORMED_SUBJECT | AUTH_UNAVAILABLE (:66-74). AUTH_UNAVAILABLE is produced in exactly two places, BOTH catch blocks around a THROW: createClient (:105-109) and getUser (:114-116). When getUser RETURNS an error object with no user, the code takes :124 and yields SESSION_REJECTED.
facts.consequence: AS-2 (provider refused the session) and AS-3 (provider unreachable or 5xx) are INDISTINGUISHABLE today, because @supabase/ssr reports a transport failure as a RETURNED AuthRetryableFetchError rather than a throw. The enumeration names four states the module does not derive. This is defect B-1 exactly, and it confirms the ratified package's implementation_consequence_stated_plainly: any implementation lane 'must NOT assume the existing AUTH_UNAVAILABLE branch already provides one'.

OWNER_CLARIFICATIONS_IN_LANE.rule: Two derivation questions were put to the product owner in this authoring turn because their answers change the DAG's node shape and one of them turns on a compression in the mission brief. Both are recorded as CLARIFICATIONS of the already-ratified package, not as new owner decisions and not as amendments to docs/ops/owner-ratifications/M11_HEALTH_CONTRACT_OWNER_DECISIONS_v1.0.0.json.

clarifications.subject: The scope of the 503 prohibition on EP-1
clarifications.why_asked: The mission brief states '503 prohibited' without qualification. The ratified authority scopes the prohibition to AS-2 specifically: docs/ops/release/M11_HEALTH_CONTRACT_ADJUDICATION_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json OWNER_DECISIONS_AFTER_AMENDMENT.decisions[OD-1].NB-3_rejected_session_semantics.constraint - 'Whatever is chosen must NOT be 503, because AS-2 proves the provider is reachable' - restated in docs/ops/owner-ratifications/M11_HEALTH_CONTRACT_OWNER_DECISIONS_v1.0.0.json ratifications[OD-1].owner_selected_decision.AS-2_503_prohibition_preserved. Reading the prohibition globally would leave EP-1 with no failing status, which would make M11-SC-8 vacuous and contradict docs/ops/owner-ratifications/M11_HEALTH_CONTRACT_OWNER_DECISIONS_v1.0.0.json ratifications[OD-5].owner_selected_decision.sequencing, which relies on A2 'giving EP-1 a genuinely failable anonymous cell'.
clarifications.owner_answer: 503_FOR_AS-3_ONLY. 503 remains PROHIBITED for AS-2. 503 is the EP-1 answer for AS-3 (provider unreachable or 5xx), which the ratified taxonomy calls 'the only one of the four that is a health fact'.
clarifications.effective_contract: AS-1 -> 200 unauthenticated body; AS-2 -> 200 unauthenticated body; AS-3 -> 503 degraded body; AS-4 -> not an EP-1 verdict at all (pre-handler platform failure, S-5).
clarifications.status: OWNER_CLARIFICATION_CONSISTENT_WITH_THE_RATIFIED_SCOPE. It relaxes nothing: the AS-2 prohibition is preserved verbatim. Independent certification should confirm this reading against the brief's flat wording.

clarifications.subject: The substrate of the OD-1 rider's cache
clarifications.why_asked: The rider fixes the PROPERTIES (short TTL, own bounded budget, not every anonymous request forcing a fresh call) but not the substrate, and the two candidate substrates have materially different failure modes.
clarifications.owner_answer: IN_PROCESS_MODULE_CACHE. A module-scope cache with a declared TTL inside the touch module, with at most one in-flight upstream call coalesced.
clarifications.rejected_and_why: A KV-backed shared cache was rejected. It would make the public liveness surface depend on the same substrate F-M11-20 measured as ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT and FAIL-OPEN, and which docs/ops/owner-ratifications/M11_HEALTH_CONTRACT_OWNER_DECISIONS_v1.0.0.json ratifications[OD-4].owner_selected_decision.rate_limiter_security_posture records as 'NOT a security control M11 may rely upon'.
clarifications.accepted_consequence: The cache is PER-INSTANCE. With N warm serverless instances the upstream call rate is bounded by N per TTL window, not by 1. This is a bounded, declared property, not an unbounded one, and TA-04 records it as such rather than claiming a global bound the substrate cannot provide.
clarifications.status: OWNER_CLARIFICATION_WITHIN_THE_RATIFIED_RIDER. Adds no constraint the rider did not already impose and removes none.

nodes.name: AUTH_FAILURE_DISCRIMINATOR
contract: Derive AS-1, AS-2, AS-3 and AS-4 from the ACTUAL error value, not from whether it was thrown. The taxonomy's measured discriminators are: AS-1 error.name AuthSessionMissingError, status 400, zero outbound attempts; AS-2 error.name AuthApiError carrying the provider's own 4xx; AS-3 error.name AuthRetryableFetchError, status 0 for transport and the provider's 5xx otherwise; AS-4 a THROW of SupabaseProjectCoherenceError.

Expose the derived state as a NEW named field on the existing result shape. The existing AuthIdentityFailure union and every existing consumer's behaviour are FROZEN by TA-02 - this node adds information, it does not re-route any existing branch.
Never echo the error message, the token, the cookie or the subject. S-1 and S-2 both already enforce upstream-text absence and this node must not regress it.
done_when: A named exported discriminator exists and is unit-tested against a constructed instance of each of the four error shapes.
AS-2 and AS-3 produce DIFFERENT derived states from inputs that both arrive as a returned error with no user - the specific conflation S-4 measured.
No existing call site's status code changes (proved by TA-02).
nodes.notes: S-4 is the whole reason this node exists: the module already NAMES four states and derives two. This node closes the gap between the enumeration and the derivation.

nodes.name: DISCRIMINATOR_NON_REGRESSION_AT_EP2_EP3
contract: EP-2 and EP-3 keep their session gate and their anonymous 401 EXACTLY as S-2 and S-3 measured them. TA-01 must not become a reason to change either route's authentication boundary or its status mapping.
The only EP-3 status change authorized anywhere in this DAG is TA-07, and it is an OD-3 status split, not a boundary change.
done_when: A control asserts EP-2 answers 401 anonymously and EP-3 answers 401 anonymously, after TA-01 lands.
nodes.notes: MG-4 forbids lowering the boundary to make measurement convenient. This node is the standing guard that TA-01's new information does not leak into the boundary.

nodes.name: PROVIDER_HEALTH_TOUCH_MODULE
surface: lib/health/provider-touch.ts (NEW - a lib module, NOT an app/** route)
contract: A sessionless probe of the Auth provider's reachability, returning a three-valued verdict: REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is a first-class value for 'budget exhausted or not yet probed', never coerced to REACHABLE.

It MUST be a lib module and MUST NOT be a new route under app/**. Two independent reasons: (a) docs/ops/release/RELEASE_GATE_LEDGER_v1.0.0.json GATES[M11].source_of_truth enumerates exactly three files and M11-SC-3 requires all three to be observed on every run - a fourth health endpoint would be a surface the gate does not name, and adding it would require a ledger edit this DAG does not authorize; (b) a new app/** entry point moves the tests/database-runtime-entrypoints.test.ts:851 inventory count, which TA-18 holds frozen.
It MUST NOT open a database connection and MUST NOT read tenant data, so that EP-1's `reaching` classification in the entry-point inventory is unchanged.
The probe target and transport must be injectable, so that TA-16 can exercise it with no real egress (S-12).
It must never expose the provider URL, a key, a token or upstream error text in any value it returns.
done_when: The module exists, is imported by EP-1 only, and its verdict type has three inhabitants.
A unit control proves UNKNOWN is never reported as REACHABLE.
tests/database-runtime-entrypoints.test.ts:851 is unchanged (TA-18).
nodes.notes: The taxonomy is explicit that a discriminator ALONE cannot give an anonymous caller provider-health information, because for an anonymous caller getUser makes no outbound call. TA-01 and TA-03 are two separate pieces of work and neither substitutes for the other.

nodes.name: TOUCH_CACHE_AND_TTL
contract: A module-scope cache with a DECLARED TTL of 15000 ms (OC-2), exported as a named constant so a test can assert the bound rather than infer it.
At most one in-flight upstream probe at a time; concurrent callers coalesce onto it (SINGLE_FLIGHT_COALESCED).

The invariant the rider states: no implementation may make every single anonymous health request necessarily cause a fresh upstream provider call. A control must prove that N requests inside one TTL window produce exactly ONE upstream call.

DECLARED STALENESS. Within one TTL window EP-1 may answer 200 from cache after the provider has actually failed. This is inherent to the rider, is bounded by TTL_MS, and is recorded here as a property of the contract rather than discovered later as a defect.
DECLARED SCOPE. The cache is PER-INSTANCE (OC-2). With N warm instances the bound is N upstream calls per TTL window, not 1. No node in this DAG may claim a global bound.
done_when: TTL_MS is an exported constant equal to 15000.
A fake-timer control proves: many requests inside the window -> one upstream call; one request after expiry -> a second upstream call.
A control proves concurrent callers coalesce rather than each probing.

nodes.name: TOUCH_INDEPENDENT_REQUEST_BUDGET
contract: A bounded request budget OWNED BY THE TOUCH, distinct from and not assumed to be covered by the OD-4 global rate limit. The rider states this explicitly.

It MUST NOT be implemented on top of the proxy.ts limiter, and MUST NOT depend on KV_REST_API_URL / KV_REST_API_TOKEN. S-6 measured that limiter as environment-dependent and fail-open, and the ratification records it as not a control M11 may rely upon.
FAIL-CLOSED DIRECTION. When the budget is exhausted the touch returns UNKNOWN - never REACHABLE. An exhausted budget must never be able to manufacture a healthy verdict.
How EP-1 renders UNKNOWN is fixed by TA-06, not here.
done_when: A named budget bound exists as an exported constant.
A control proves budget exhaustion yields UNKNOWN and never REACHABLE.
A control proves the touch reads neither KV environment variable.
nodes.notes: This is the single node most likely to be quietly skipped, because a cache alone already 'feels' like a budget. The rider names them as two constraints and this DAG keeps them as two nodes.

nodes.name: EP1_PUBLIC_LIVENESS_RESPONSE_CONTRACT
contract: AS-1 -> 200 with an unauthenticated body. AS-2 -> 200 with an unauthenticated body; a rejected session is treated as simply not-authenticated. 503 is PROHIBITED for AS-2 - unconditionally, and this DAG does not relax it.

AS-3 -> 503 with a degraded body (OC-1). AS-3 is the only one of the four that is a health fact, and it is the state that makes the anonymous EP-1 cell genuinely failable, which is what M11-SC-8 requires and what OD-5's sequencing relies on.
AS-4 -> NOT an EP-1 verdict. By S-5 it is raised in middleware before the handler runs and is recorded once per deployment under PLATFORM_PRE_HANDLER_FAILURE_RULE.
An authenticated caller keeps 200 and authenticated:true. The PII rule is unchanged: no user identifier, email, provider name, token, cookie or upstream error text, ever.
The body must carry the upstream verdict as an explicit field so the runner can compare a cell rather than a bare numeral (M11-SC-4).
done_when: A control per AS state fixes the exact status AND the exact body discriminator.
A MUST-FAIL control proves AS-2 can never produce 503.

A control proves an anonymous request against an unreachable provider produces a DIFFERENT observable answer than against a reachable one - the property F-M11-13 records as absent today and M11-SC-8 requires.
nodes.notes: This node is what converts EP-1 from a constant-answer cell into a failable one. Everything upstream of it (TA-01, TA-03, TA-04, TA-05) exists to make this node's AS-3 branch derivable at all.

nodes.name: EP3_INTENTIONAL_OFF_STATUS_SPLIT
contract: Intentional-off - master.stellaEnabled false - answers 200. A subsystem expected to be on whose precondition is unmet answers 503, as today.

NO NEW BODY FIELD. S-3 confirms the body at :82-118 already distinguishes the two cases via master.stellaEnabled, master.geminiApiKeyPresent, master.canUseStella and rateLimit. Only the status mapping at :123 changes.

PRECEDENCE MUST BE EXPLICIT. When stellaEnabled is false AND rateLimit.satisfied is false, intentional-off DOMINATES and the answer is 200. A deliberately dark subsystem is not made unhealthy by a precondition of the thing that is switched off.

DECLARED CONSEQUENCE: after this node, status 200 on EP-3 NO LONGER IMPLIES ready:true. `ready` remains false for an intentionally-off deployment while the status is 200. Any caller that branches on status alone will read intentional-off as ready. This is the direct cost of the owner's selection and it is recorded here, not discovered later.
The auth boundary is untouched (TA-02).
done_when: A control per quadrant of (stellaEnabled, ready) fixes the status.
A MUST-FAIL control proves a 200 with ready:false is reachable and is NOT treated as a ready deployment - the specific hazard the status split introduces.
A control fixes the precedence case (off AND unsatisfied -> 200).
nodes.notes: OD-3 carries NO provisioning cost and does not depend on OD-5, so this node is landable in the first slice.

nodes.name: OD4_PROXY_FREEZE
contract: NOT_EXEMPT is satisfied by the CURRENT code. S-6 measured that /api/health/* is already matched and already rate-limited wherever KV is bound. The ratification states no code change to proxy.ts is authorized or required.
This node is therefore a NEGATIVE node: it authorizes NO change to proxy.ts, and exists so that the OD-4 obligation is visibly discharged rather than silently assumed.
No implementation in this DAG may add a health-path exemption, change the window, change the key, or change the fail-open catch.
done_when: proxy.ts blob is unchanged at 4296e2c2bd85f071c2b248c109396c4f0b133183 when the Track A slice lands.
A control asserts /api/health/* is within config.matcher and is not special-cased.
nodes.notes: Recorded as a node precisely because 'no change required' is the kind of obligation an implementation lane forgets to prove.

nodes.name: M11_RUNNER_CORE
surface: scripts/ or tests/ runner surface (NEW) plus a deploy-smoke workflow (NEW)
contract: An automated runner that observes ALL THREE endpoints on every deployment (M11-SC-3 - a skipped endpoint is a FAIL, not a partial PASS).

Each observation is compared against THE CELL FOR THE RUNNER'S OWN CALLER CLASS (M11-SC-4), never against a single global expectation. For an unauthenticated runner, 401 from EP-2 and EP-3 is the CONFORMANT answer.
Every observation is bound to the deployment identifier AND the exact SHA SERVED - not the SHA requested (M11-SC-5).
S-10 measured that no runner and no deploy-smoke workflow exist, and that the Golden Journey observes no health endpoint. This is a new surface, not an extension of golden-journey.yml.
done_when: The runner exists, runs on every deployment, and emits a cell-by-cell record bound to deployment id and served SHA.
nodes.notes: FIS-M11-05 (hosted-smoke ACCESS to a protected deployment) is a RECORDED DEPENDENCY of any hosted run, not part of Track A's landable scope, and is not authorized here.

nodes.name: RUNNER_INCONCLUSIVE_SEMANTICS
contract: 429 from the global rate limit is ALWAYS recorded INCONCLUSIVE. Never a PASS, never a health FAIL - unconditionally, regardless of environment, deployment or caller class. OD-4's NOT_EXEMPT makes 429 a live reachable outcome on every health path, which is exactly why the disposition is unconditional.
302 from Deployment Protection and any transport error are likewise INCONCLUSIVE.

PLATFORM FAILURE IS ONE INCIDENT, NOT THREE VERDICTS. If every matched health path returns the same platform-level failure in one run, the runner MUST record ONE platform incident bound to the deployment identifier and SHA, and record the run INCONCLUSIVE for every endpoint. It must NOT record three FAILs.

THE WIRE NUMERAL FOR A MIDDLEWARE THROW IS UNMEASURED. The ratified rule is written on the SHAPE of the failure - identical across all matched paths, before any handler - and explicitly not on a numeral. An implementation lane MUST measure the numeral against a real deployment before encoding it. This DAG does not supply it and does not authorize measuring it.
done_when: A control proves 429 maps to INCONCLUSIVE and can reach neither PASS nor FAIL.
A control proves three identical platform-level failures in one run produce ONE incident record, not three FAILs.
A MUST-FAIL control proves an INCONCLUSIVE run cannot satisfy the gate.

BLOCKING is PRESERVED as the target semantics for when the precondition IS met. This is sequencing, not a change to the owner's EP-2 = BLOCKING selection.
EP-2 MAY NOT SILENTLY PASS BEFORE TRACK B EXISTS. This is a hard invariant of Track A and is proved by a must-fail control, not by review.
